video_title: Why a Crypto VC Would Choose Solana Over Ethereum
gist: Sixman Ventures' Mike Dudis argues memecoins are a permanent crypto primitive whose 'attention/community' valuation ethos is bleeding into collectibles, meme stocks and AI assets, and that the real 2026 opportunity is getting higher-quality assets (RWAs, tokenized equities, collectibles) onchain. He states his fund is positioned SOL-over-ETH as an asset on activity growth from a lower base, expects Robinhood chain's memecoin phase to peter out, and thinks most crypto-AI/compute value will accrue to equity rather than tokens.

themes.theme: Bonk as the memecoin airdrop blueprint

insights.claim: Bonk was launched in late 2022 by a group of roughly 20 people who airdropped about 50% of supply to Solana developers, users and NFT collectors as a deliberate stimulus at the post-FTX bottom, when SOL was near $10.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: A template for reviving a dormant ecosystem: broad retroactive airdrops to actual builders can restart activity cheaper than grants or incentives — watch for copycats at future cycle bottoms.
insights.quote: there was a meme at the time a joke that there were something like 75 developers left in Salana

insights.claim: Bonk's airdrop went from zero to a token trading above roughly $400 million market value within about a month to six weeks, putting a couple hundred million dollars into Solana builders' hands at the ecosystem's low point.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Quantifies how fast a well-targeted community airdrop can manufacture balance-sheet wealth and sentiment in a beaten-down ecosystem.
insights.quote: air dropped you know 50% of supply within I think like a month or six weeks the token was trading over 400 million

insights.claim: Solana Mobile loaded more than $1,000 of Bonk onto its phone, effectively making the hardware free for buyers who sold the token — a memecoin used as a hardware customer-acquisition subsidy.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Token-subsidized hardware/user acquisition is a repeatable go-to-market that traditional CAC math can't match; watch for it in consumer crypto device and app launches.

insights.claim: Bonk survived by converting from a pure memecoin into an operating project with products — Bonk Swap, NFT sets, a memecoin launchpad — plus a core team that gives grants and invests in Solana projects.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: The durable memecoins are the ones that back into products and treasuries; screen memecoin exposure for whether a real product/team exists behind the ticker.

insights.claim: There is no rational valuation framework that can model what memecoins should be worth, so they are permanently speculative and should only be held by people who enjoy the underlying community.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Frames memecoin allocation as an entertainment/consumption budget rather than a modellable position — sizing, not analysis, is the only risk control.
insights.quote: there's no like rational valuation framework, you know, that's going to fit into a model that I can put together to tell you what these things should be worth

insights.claim: Memecoins hold a disproportionately large share of crypto's genuinely valuable assets relative to L1s, L2s and infrastructure tokens, because good assets are rare across every crypto subsector.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Argues the hit rate on memecoins is not worse than on infra tokens — a reason to stop excluding the category outright from crypto portfolios.
insights.quote: actually memecoins have a pretty good share of the quote unquote good or highly valued assets relative to, you know, L1's, L2s, infra, you name it

insights.claim: Mimetic and attention-based pricing is no longer crypto-specific: meme stocks and 'virtually everything in the AI economy' now trade on sentiment and are hard to tie back to fundamentals.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: If attention-value is the cross-asset regime, fundamental screens will keep underperforming in both crypto and AI equities; narrative/flow indicators become the live edge.

insights.claim: Even the best NFT collections such as CryptoPunks are down roughly 90% from peak, yet holders still value the community and IP — the same logic that makes memecoin drawdowns tolerable to their communities.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Sets a realistic base rate for community-asset drawdowns: expect ~90% declines even in survivors, so position sizes must assume it.

themes.theme: The Anom coin experiment vs. Trump-coin extraction

insights.claim: Dudis is an investor in Bullpen, the company Anom co-founded, and personally owns some of the Anom memecoin, but says it is explicitly not an asset suitable for his fund because he runs a registered investment adviser.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: A clean example of the RIA constraint that keeps institutional capital out of memecoins even when the manager is personally bullish — a structural cap on the category's institutional bid.
insights.quote: it's not for example an asset that's suitable for our fund. You know I run a fund and I'm a registered investment adviser.

insights.claim: Anom did not launch his memecoin — the supply was gifted to him at zero, he has bought as it rose and has not sold, and he is publicly staking his entire reputation on it, which distinguishes it from extractive celebrity launches.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Insider sell behavior, not the meme itself, is the variable that separates survivable creator coins from dumps — track founder wallet flows as the primary signal.
insights.quote: He's staking his entire reputation extremely publicly on this thing succeeding.

insights.claim: The Trump coin was structured with a single-sided liquidity pool and influencer promotion so insiders could sell into retail buying for cash regardless of long-term performance, and it effectively topped the memecoin market.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Names the specific mechanism (single-sided LP + paid attention) that marks a token as extractive — a screenable red flag before entry.
insights.quote: they were selling the Trump coin into that for cash and and made a tremendous amount of money regardless of how the thing performed long term

insights.claim: The Anom model promises to share value from other business initiatives with token holders but explicitly will not confer equity in Anom's companies or in Bullpen, leaving holders with a mimetic claim rather than a legal one.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Defines the risk: holders are betting on voluntary value-sharing, not enforceable rights — pricing should carry a large discount to any equity-like comparison.

themes.theme: Base backlash vs. Robinhood chain rotation

insights.claim: Base's problem was timing, not evil intent: it leaned into memecoins, AI coins and creator coins right at the market top, and creator coins specifically were a tone-deaf idea that was never going to work.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Reframes the Base-is-bad narrative as cycle timing — useful when assessing whether the ecosystem's fundamentals or just its launch window failed.
insights.quote: those were never going to work that was just a really bad tonedeaf idea uh with bad timing

insights.claim: Robinhood chain will not be a durable memecoin chain — the memecoin activity there is expected to plateau and peter out, with the Vlad-hack copycat token that lost people money already showing how fast it degrades.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: A fadeable narrative: positioning for Robinhood chain as the next memecoin venue is likely to mean-revert; the durable story there is RWAs, not memes.
insights.quote: my guess is the activity there sort of plateaus and peters out and that's probably a good thing

insights.claim: Tokenized RWA ownership on Robinhood chain is increasing rapidly, and Robinhood's real strategic logic is that memecoin attention funnels users toward discovering better assets they can be directed into.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Memecoins as a top-of-funnel acquisition channel for regulated products is the reusable playbook — watch RWA volume, not meme volume, as the Robinhood chain KPI.

insights.claim: Solana's core weakness for the last few years has been a shortage of quality assets on chain, which is why bundlers can launch thousands of throwaway tokens per day and users keep churning through them.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Asset quality — not throughput — is the binding constraint on Solana user retention; track RWA/equity issuance on Solana as the fix that would rerate the chain.
insights.quote: That's been Salana's issue for the last few years uh is that we just don't have enough quality assets on the chain

themes.theme: SOL over ETH as an asset

insights.claim: Sixman Ventures is positioned as a Solana-bullish fund at the asset level while still holding many investments across the Ethereum and EVM builder ecosystem — an explicit separation of asset allocation from ecosystem exposure.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Shows a VC splitting the token trade from the venture book — you can be short the L1 token thesis and long the ecosystem's companies.

insights.claim: With Ethereum at roughly a $225 billion market cap versus Solana around $43 billion, Dudis takes SOL over ETH for a five-year hold because SOL has better properties given that value differential.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: A concrete relative-value call with the spread stated; the ~5x cap differential is the margin of safety being cited for the SOL/ETH ratio trade.
insights.quote: I just believe that soul has better properties than ETH particularly given the value differential

insights.claim: Ethereum's TVL and total value issued lead is attributed largely to inertia and loyalty from historic wealth creation, and those loyalties will not exist among the general population if crypto scales 10-100x.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: If ETH's lead is a legacy-holder effect rather than a preference, new-user growth is structurally SOL-favorable — a testable thesis via net-new address cohorts.

insights.claim: SOL is expected to trade on a momentum-and-activity narrative over the next 24 months, driven by much faster stablecoin volume growth and perps finally succeeding on Solana from a near-zero base.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Gives specific trackable KPIs for the SOL thesis — Solana stablecoin volume and perps DEX volume are the confirmation/invalidation metrics.
insights.quote: soul will trade on a momentum narrative over the next 24 months would be my guess based on more activity happening on the chain

insights.claim: Asked what he would do as Ethereum's CEO, Dudis would lean into ETH-as-money across L2s and recruit large fintechs — Robinhood, Coinbase, Revolut — onto L2s while persuading them not to launch standalone L1s like Tempo, since ETH will trade on narrative rather than L1 fee capture.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: The ETH bull case to monitor is enterprise L2 announcements, not L1 fee revenue; a major fintech choosing an independent L1 like Tempo is the bear signal.
insights.quote: I'd lean heavily into Robin Hood. I'd do things that Salana can't do.

insights.claim: Consumer crypto is the most contrarian category right now because everyone is chasing the institutional RWA/tokenized-securities trade, and consumer is the class that takes longest to develop since infrastructure must build up first.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Identifies where VC competition is lowest; consumer crypto entry points now price in the least optimism.

insights.claim: Collectibles are the first consumer category migrating on chain, with companies like Collector, Courtyard and an OpenSea pivoting into 'the eBay of collectibles' — and Sixman invested in Trove in Q4 of last year, which is doing very well.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Names the specific private comps in the onchain collectibles trade and a disclosed position — a map for tracking the sector's private rounds.
insights.quote: We made an investment there in a company called Trove uh in Q4 of last year.

insights.claim: Tokenized collectibles are a roughly 10x better expression of what PFP NFTs attempted in 2021-22 because the IP is decades-old and pre-validated by society rather than newly invented.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Lindy IP plus poor legacy market structure (eBay) is the screen for which real-world asset classes migrate onchain first.
insights.quote: it was like a Charizard. It just has more brand.

insights.claim: Pokemon cards and memecoins share the same ethos and overlapping status/scarcity valuation logic, but differ critically in that memecoins are infinitely divisible while cards are not.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Divisibility, not legitimacy, is the real structural difference — it explains why memecoins have far larger holder counts but weaker per-unit scarcity value.

insights.claim: In-game digital goods spending by children on Roblox and Fortnite skins will eventually become tradeable as those closed businesses top out in addressable market, creating a 'game coins' category.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Watch for gaming platforms opening secondary markets as growth stalls — the trigger would be a large step-change in tokenized consumer asset supply.

insights.claim: Crypto has had three years to produce non-financial consumer products — gaming, streaming coins — and none of it materialized, which is why the majority of onchain activity is still in the memecoin trenches.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Memecoin dominance is a symptom of a product vacuum; the trade rotates only when a durable consumer product ships, not when sentiment turns.
insights.quote: we've had three years to produce other things for consumers and other things of like social value that they could spend their time on, whether it be gaming, whether it be streaming coins, and you know, none of that stuff's materialized

insights.claim: Non-US users can already trade tokenized SpaceX, Tesla and AI super-cycle exposure on chain permissionlessly with no KYC, which is the asset-quality upgrade that could retain consumers arriving through memecoins.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Geo-blocked tokenized equities are the live wedge for ex-US retail onboarding; volume there is an early indicator of the RWA thesis working.

insights.claim: Crypto's value is accruing to equity holders and to incumbents like Stripe and PayPal rather than to native tokens, and reversing that will take a long time despite experiments now underway.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Argues the better risk-adjusted exposure to crypto's build-out this cycle is private/public equity, not liquid tokens.

insights.claim: The market is not yet rewarding token transparency or ownership rights: MetaDAO's ownership coins get downside protection but no valuation premium or breakout, despite Blockworks pushing its transparency framework industry-wide.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Evidence that cash-flow/rights disclosure is not yet a rerating catalyst for tokens — don't underwrite 'transparency premium' theses on current data.
insights.quote: we're investors in Metadow and they have ownership coins

insights.claim: Even Pump, known as a memecoin launchpad, now runs an ACE platform where launched tokens can confer equity-like rights to holders, showing the whole spectrum experimenting with better-quality onchain assets.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Launchpads converging on equity-like token rights is the leading edge of the token-quality trade; early platforms could capture the issuance flow.
insights.quote: even pump which you know is known as a memecoin launchpad has their ace platform where you can launch a token and then you can have that token confer uh equity-like rights um to the holders

insights.claim: Crypto will be redefined as financial infrastructure and ledgers rather than native assets, with only a handful of special assets — Bitcoin, probably Ethereum and Solana — retaining that status while tokens like Hype and Pump trade as equity-like on business performance.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Implies a bifurcated token market: monetary-premium assets versus cash-flow-multiple assets — valuation method should be chosen per bucket, not per sector.
insights.quote: I think things like Hype and Pump, you will be much much more tied to business performance and look equity like

insights.claim: Stablecoins and public permissionless rails could produce the first trillion-dollar-plus financial services company within the next 5 to 10 years, a scale that has never existed in the sector.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: The largest stated upside in the episode sits in stablecoin-rail equities, not tokens — relevant for private-market and pre-IPO positioning.
insights.quote: we'll have the first trillion dollar plus uh you financial services company

themes.theme: Cycle, regulation, AI and time horizons

insights.claim: This cycle has been lower-volatility — it did not go as high as expected and has not gone as low as it feels — and that compression is expected to continue as Bitcoin halvings lose impact and the four-year cycle breaks down.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: A structurally lower-amplitude cycle changes position sizing and drawdown assumptions for crypto beta; the four-year model is losing predictive power.
insights.quote: We didn't go as high, not as low.

insights.claim: The Clarity Act has not passed and now looks unlikely to, largely due to the Trump family's ethics conflicts and bank pushback against yield-bearing onchain dollars, but that failure is already somewhat priced in.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Removes a widely-cited catalyst/risk from the market-level view while leaving asset-specific regulatory risk (e.g. Hyperliquid) unresolved.
insights.quote: it just feels like Clarity not passing is somewhat priced in

insights.claim: Dudis expects it to feel clear by early next year that the market has the wind at its back, regardless of the regulatory outcome, supported by stablecoin finance, RWA issuance, perps and prediction markets as new themes.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: A dated, falsifiable market call with named drivers — early 2027 is the checkpoint for this thesis.
insights.quote: by early next year, uh, it's going to feel clear that we have sort of the wind at our sales

insights.claim: Most value in crypto-AI and compute markets today involves no tokens at all — crypto-native founders behind companies like Nous Research and OpenRouter deliberately avoid tokens and downplay their crypto backgrounds when pitching AI.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Deflates the AI-token trade: exposure to crypto's AI talent is via equity, and 'AI x crypto' tokens should be discounted accordingly.
insights.quote: when you're talking to folks in the AI industry, you know, you don't lead with the fact that you've come from crypto markets

insights.claim: Compute markets will mostly develop off-chain and OTC because compute is extremely bespoke across data centers, but crypto primitives — especially novel credit markets and capital formation like USDe-style lending pools — will participate in the buildout.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Points the AI-crypto trade at onchain credit and capital formation for data centers rather than at compute-marketplace tokens.

insights.claim: AI's current growth is substantially funded by non-economic activity — continuous fundraising and products offered below profitability — raising the question of how long it can continue, just as an AI safety-review backlash (Demis-style FINRA-like review) is forming.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Two compounding risks to AI-linked equities and tokens over the next year or two: funding dependency plus a regulatory slowdown.
insights.quote: right now AI is is growing a lot due to noneconomic activity just to you know fundraising and the ability to continually fund raise and in many cases offer products um you know below profitability

insights.claim: Four-year boom-bust cycles are the core obstacle to building financial infrastructure because they burn out users, investors and builders, so better onchain assets that smooth investor behavior would compound into greater retention.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Frames asset quality as the mechanism that damps cycle amplitude — a reason lower volatility and RWA growth are the same trade.
insights.quote: it's really really difficult to build out new financial infrastructure when you're operating on these like four-year boom and bust cycles

insights.claim: Adoption timelines should be modelled in 20-plus years rather than six, using AI as the analogy — Kurzweil's predictions took 25 years to arrive and Tether was widely called a scam five or six years ago before becoming one of the world's largest companies.
insights.speaker: Mike Dudis
insights.so_what: Calibrates disillusionment: the gap between narrative and delivery is normal and typically resolves in an abrupt step-change, favoring patient capital.
